steps.description: Victim submits a swap of 100 ETH for USDC with a 5% slippage tolerance (minAmountOut set to ~$190,000). This transaction is visible in the public mempool. The attacker's MEV bot detects the large pending swap and calculates the optimal sandwich parameters.

state_changes.victim_tx_status: ⚠️ Pending in mempool (visible to MEV bots)

steps.description: Attacker front-runs the victim by submitting a large buy with higher gas priority. They swap 500 ETH for USDC, moving the price significantly. The pool reserves shift from 10,000/20M to 10,500/~19,048,000. The effective ETH price rises from $2,000 to ~$2,177 due to the constant product formula.

steps.action: swap(100 ETH → USDC) [EXECUTES at worse price]
steps.description: Victim's transaction executes at the now-inflated price. Instead of receiving ~$200,000 USDC at the original price, they receive only ~$190,476 due to the attacker's front-run. The victim loses ~$9,524 but the transaction still succeeds because the output exceeds their 5% slippage minimum of $190,000.

Immediately after the victim's swap, the attacker back-runs by swapping their USDC back to ETH. The pool is now skewed with extra ETH, so the attacker gets a favorable rate. They recover ~505 ETH for their 952,381 USDC, netting ~5 ETH profit (~$10,000).

The sandwich attack is complete in a single block. The attacker spent 500 ETH and recovered ~506 ETH, netting ~6 ETH (~$12,000) in profit. The victim received $9,524 less than the fair market price. The attacker paid ~$200 in gas fees, making this highly profitable MEV extraction.
